The **Enterprise segment** offers the strongest growth quality, as it shows the best performance across satisfaction, churn, and expansion metrics, but it demands more implementation capacity due to long, complex onboarding.

- **Satisfaction:** Enterprise clients show the highest NPS of **52** once fully onboarded [NL-011-S08], [NL-012-S03], [NL-016-S03].
- **Churn:** Enterprise accounts exhibit the lowest monthly logo churn at **1.3%** [NL-012-S03], [NL-016-S03], [NL-015-S03], compared to 2.1% for Mid-Market and 4.8% for SMB.
- **Expansion:** Enterprise generated **$91,000** in expansion revenue in Q2 2026, representing **52.6%** of all expansion revenue [NL-012-S03], [NL-016-S03], [NL-012-S05]. This is driven by multi-department scaling and custom SSO/compliance add-ons [NL-012-S05]. Enterprise also has the highest LTV:CAC ratio of **16.0x** vs 8.3x for SMB [NL-016-S03].
- **Implementation capacity requirement:** Enterprise onboarding averages **8.7 weeks** [NL-012-S03], [NL-016-S03], [NL-015-S03] due to permission-mapping challenges, security reviews, and integration with legacy knowledge systems [NL-012-S03], [NL-016-S03]. Enterprise clients are vulnerable to delays during the implementation phase and require dedicated CSM support, detailed compliance reviews, custom DPAs, and audit log retention windows [NL-011-S08]. This long onboarding duration makes customer onboarding a **resource constraint**, necessitating automated tools to streamline permission mapping and improve the initial document cleanup process [NL-012-S09].
